newsitem.title: UK: UK loosens grip on Inntrepreneur pubs.
newsitem.headline: UK loosens grip on Inntrepreneur pubs.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said on Wednesday that it would release the Inntrepreneur pub estate from certain restrictions. But Inntrepreneur, owned jointly by Grand Metropolitan Plc and Fosters, should no longer require its pub tenants to take beer exclusively from Scottish & Newcastle which owns the Courage brands, said the government department.

S&N currently supplies beer to all of Inntrepreneur's estate of pubs which expires in March 1998. The new undertaking requires Inntrepreneur to offer more choice of beers to its tenants after March 1998.

The merger between Fosters and Grand Metropolitan was completed in 1991. It involved Courage, formerly owned by Fosters until the sale of Courage to S&N in 1995, acquiring the brewing interests of GrandMet and the creation of a combined pub estate known as Inntrepreneur Estates.

At the time of the merger Inntrepreneur owned about 8,500 pubs, which included 1,750 GrandMet operated Chef & Brewer managed pubs. Inntrepeneur's estate has since been reduced to 2,900, similar in size to other pub chains like Greenalls and Pubmaster.
The DTI said it no longer required Inntrepreneur to have a tied estate of no more than 4,350 pubs or free any pubs it still owns from tie by 1998.
Tied pubs are owned by the brewer who requires the tenant to sell only its own beers on the premises.

"The nature and size of Inntrepreneur are now similar to a number of other pub chain operators, therefore it is no longer appropriate to maintain the existing undertakings in force," said Taylor in a statement.
The DTI also said Inntrepreneur does not have to allow its pubs to take a so-called guest beer or own no more than 20 percent of pubs in any one licensing district.
Under the Beer Orders 1991 tied tenants of national brewers are required to sell a cask conditioned ale from a brewer outside the tie.
